transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I guess since I stopped working, I’ve had a harder time just… slowing down. It’s not a big crisis or anything, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’m up and moving all day, going from one little job to the next around the house. Kind of like I still have a crew waiting on me, if that makes sense.
During these times when you can’t slow down, do you also feel unusually upbeat or energized compared with your normal self?

I don’t think so, no… not like unusually upbeat or anything. I mean, I might feel a little better when I’m getting things done, but I wouldn’t say it’s some big burst of energy or not feeling like myself. It’s more just… I keep moving. Does that answer what you’re asking?
When you try to sit still, do unwanted thoughts keep pushing into your mind until you get up and do something?

Not so much unwanted thoughts, I don’t think. It’s more physical, if that makes sense. Like if I’m sitting through a quiet meeting or a church talk, I’ll catch myself shifting around, tapping my foot, wanting to stand up and stretch even though I know I ought to just sit still. It’s not terrible, but it is hard to stay put sometimes.
When you were a child, were you also the kind of person who had a hard time sitting still?

Yeah… I suppose I was, though I don’t want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything. In grade school, teachers would say I was bright, but kind of scattered. I’d lose pencils, blurt out answers sometimes, and they’d have to remind me to finish my work before recess. Things like that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things?

I don’t think I worry a lot, no. I mean, I have the normal concerns anyone has, bills or health stuff now and then, but I wouldn’t say it takes over my day or anything like that. At least, I don’t think so.
Did these restlessness problems start after you stopped working?

Yes, I’d say that’s when it became more noticeable. I mean, I probably had little bits of it before, but it became a real problem after I retired from handyman work… about a year and two months ago, I guess. I had less to keep me moving, and sitting around more made it stand out.
Do these problems with restlessness or being scattered get in the way of your daily life?

A little, yeah… I mean, I manage okay most of the time, but it has caused some problems. My wife’s sort of taken over keeping the calendar and checking behind me, which I appreciate, though I don’t love admitting that. And I’ve had to apologize more than once to the community center and the garden group when I forgot something or didn’t follow through and let people down. So… yes, I guess it does get in the way some.
